newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi says economy needs "vitamins".
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi says economy needs "vitamins".

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Saturday that Italy's economy needed "a dose of vitamins" after a slowdown in 1996.
He told a public meeting in the northern city of Bologna that the economy slowed last year. "Now we need to start again by giving the economy a dose of vitamins," he said.
Prodi's words echoed those of Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio, who told a convention in Milan earlier that the slowdown already under way in 1996 had worsened at the end of the year.
"At the economic level, the level of economic activity remains unsatisfactory," Fazio said, predicting that gross domestic product (GDP) would grow by little more than one percent this year.
The government has an official target of 2.0 percent growth for 1997 but Labour Minister Tiziano Treu has said the actual figure is more likely to be 1.2 to 1.5 percent.

Prodi said the government had already begun or had planned a number of initiatives designed to kick-start growth, including measures to stimulate the construction and car industries and reforms of the school, military service and justice systems.

"I started my job eight months ago and we're already further ahead than 34 governments," Prodi added, a reference to Italy's tradition of chronically unstable politics. His centre-left Olive Tree coalition government is the 55th since World War Two.
"The Olive Tree government works seriously, well, calmly and does not fight," said Prodi, adding that he was renewing Italy "for real."
